title: Microtubule Plus-End Dynamics Visualization in Huntington's Disease Model based on Human Primary Skin Fibroblasts
protocol: Deliver the biopsy to a laboratory within a few hours in DMEM medium supplemented with penicillin and streptomycin.
Place the biopsy tissue in a 6 cm Petri dish together with a small amount of the medium.
Cut the biopsy sample into pieces of about 0.5-1 mm in size using a sterile scalpel.
Place 1-2 obtained fragments into a 3.5 cm Petri dish and cover them with a sterile coverslip.
Slowly add 1.5 mL of growth medium to the Petri dish containing the biopsy pieces.
Culture fibroblasts in the growth medium inside a CO2 incubator at 5% CO2, 37 °C, and 80% humidity.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 900 µL of cooled FBS.
Transfer the resuspended cells drop by drop into a cryopreservation tube.
Add 100 µL of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Place the cryovial in a low-temperature freezer at -80 °C.
After 24 hours, transfer the cryovial to liquid nitrogen (-196 °C) for long-term storage.
Remove the cryovial from the nitrogen storage and transfer 1 mL of its content into a 15 mL conical tube containing 9 mL of transport medium preheated to 37 °C.
Centrifuge the tube for 5 min at 200 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the required volume of growth medium.
Place the resuspended cells on a Petri dish of the required diameter.
Cover the dish bottom with autoclaved 0.1% gelatin solution prepared in distilled water.
Incubate for 15 min.
Prepare a culture medium with DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 2 mM L-alanyl-L-glutamine, and 50 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin.
Mix the culture medium thoroughly and store it at 4 °C.
Warm the culture medium to 37 °C before adding it to the cells.
Assess the cell culture under a microscope.
Remove the medium from the dish.
Wash the fibroblasts with Dulbecco's phosphate-salt solution (DPBS).
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed 0.25% trypsin solution to the cells.
Check if the cells detach from the substrate completely under the microscope.
Deactivate trypsin with 1 mL of culture medium.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 x g for 5 min, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of culture medium.
Count the number of cells.
Calculate the required number of cells to seed them with a density of 8-15 x 103/cm2 and resuspend in 2 mL of culture medium.
Remove the gelatin solution from the culture dish and immediately add 2 mL of cell suspension.
Cultivate fibroblasts at 37 °C in a CO2 incubator.
Refresh the medium every 2-4 days.
Replace the culture medium with fresh culture medium 24 h before transfection.
Prepare a DNA-lipid complex based on the area and density of the cell seeding using liposome-based transfection agent.
Add 3 µL of commercial transfection reagent to 125 µL of Opti-MEM without touching tube walls, gently resuspend.
Dilute plasmid DNA (GFP-EB3) by adding 1 µg of plasmid DNA to 125 µL of Opti-MEM, gently resuspend.
Add diluted plasmid DNA to each tube of diluted transfection reagent (1:1).
Incubate the mixture for 30 min.
Add the DNA-lipid complex to the 6 cm Petri dish containing cells and mix with a cruciform swing for 30 s.
Incubate cells with the transfection agent for 24 h.
Change to fresh medium after incubation.
Analyze the efficiency of transfection after 24 h.
Analyze the efficiency of transfection after 48 h.
Change the culture medium to a medium without pH-indicator dye before live imaging to reduce autofluorescence.
Carefully apply mineral oil to the medium surface to completely cover it, isolating it from the external environment to reduce O₂ penetration and medium evaporation.
Use a mercury lamp and oil immersion 60x or 100x objective lens with high numerical aperture to take images.
Check the level of double distilled water before filming.
Place the confocal dish with cells in the microscope holder.
Securely attach the dish and camera to the holder.
Choose low exposure values to minimize cell damage from ROS.
Focus on the object of interest for imaging.
Use an automatic focus stabilization system for long-term time-lapse imaging.
Select optimal imaging conditions based on cells' photosensitivity and fluorochrome fading rate.
Set a frame rate sufficiently high, such as 1 frame/s, to capture microtubule dynamics in skin fibroblasts.
Move away from previously imaged areas to avoid photo-bleaching effects.
Choose the optimal video for studying microtubules' dynamics visually.
Consider the quality of transfection in the selection process.
Evaluate the quality of microtubules' images for an optimal signal-to-noise ratio.
Ensure the absence of drifting in the analyzed cell.
Study microtubules' plus-ends dynamics by tracing them in ImageJ or Fiji program.
